newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CROWN DIPS BELOW FIXING ON MARK BUYING.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN DIPS BELOW FIXING ON MARK BUYING.

text.p: 1345 GMT - Czech crown drifts below Tuesday's cenbank fixing against mark/dollar basket, mostly on mark buying
* Crown at 27.302/dollar, 17.731/mark or +2.36 pct vs basket
* Dealers say mark buys driving crown back to Monday levels

The Czech crown gave back Tuesday's gains in afternoon trading as mark buying sent the Czech currency well under levels of the central bank's mid-day fixing against the mark/dollar basket, dealers said.

By 1545 CET (1345 GMT), the crown had dropped to 27.302 to the dollar and 17.731 to the mark, or 2.36 percent above parity against the basket, down from the central bank's fixing at 27.152 and 17.688, or +2.70 percent at 1130 local time.

"There is some buying interest especially on mark/Czech (crown) from London but its still in the range of trading like over the last seven or eight days," said trader Tomas Becvar at Prague's Komercni Banka.
The crown opened slightly above Monday's fixing of 27.147 and 17.736, or +2.53 percent, and was trading at +2.66 percent versus the basket when the central bank fixed the currency on Tuesday.

Dealers said they expected the crown to remain traading in a tight range around current levels or slightly weaken until November Senate elections, barring a surprise move by the government to boost exports, or a worsening in the conservative minority government's political battle with the opposition.
